title: Notices, articles & formats (CBSE/ICSE)
examples: What should I include when I write a notice?
How do I know how long an article should be?
Is there a specific way to write a notice for school?

explain.say: Today we are learning about writing different texts. We will look at notices and articles. Knowing the format is very important for your writing.
A notice needs a clear heading and the date. It must tell everyone what the notice is about quickly. For example, a lost pet notice needs a catchy title.
Articles have a title, an introduction, and main body paragraphs. The introduction should grab the reader's attention right away. For example, an article about recycling starts with the problem.
Word limits tell you how long your writing should be. If you are told to write about one hundred words, try to stick close to that number. This shows you can write concisely.
In real life, you see these formats everywhere. Think about a school assembly notice or a local newspaper article. They both follow these rules.
A common mistake is writing too much when a word limit is given. You might add extra details that do not help your main point. Always check the required word count first.

faq.q: Do I need to use fancy language in my notices?
faq.a: No, the language should be clear and direct for everyone to understand. You should use simple, straightforward words. You could also ask if formal language is needed, or what tone to use.
asks: What kind of language is appropriate?

faq.q: If I write an article, should I use headings?
faq.a: Yes, using subheadings helps organize your thoughts for the reader. It makes the article look professional and easy to read. You could also ask if paragraphs are enough, or how to structure sections.
asks: How do I break up long text?

faq.q: What if the notice is for a very small group?
faq.a: Even for a small group, the format remains the same. You still need a clear heading, date, and all necessary details. You could also ask if the audience changes the format, or if I need to address people directly.
asks: Does the audience matter for the format?
Can I skip the date if it is for a class?

faq.q: How do I know exactly how many words I have?
faq.a: You should count every single word you write, including short connecting words. Use a word processor's word count tool if you are typing it. You could also ask for a word counter, or how to check the total count.
asks: Is punctuation counted as a word?
What counts towards the word total?

faq.q: Can I use bullet points in an article?
faq.a: It is better to write in full sentences for an article. Bullet points are usually best reserved for very short notices or lists of items. You could also ask if it breaks the flow, or if it is acceptable in the body.
asks: Are bullet points okay in articles?
When should I use lists instead of paragraphs?

facts: A notice must always include the name of the issuing authority.
Articles should have a clear introduction to hook the reader.
Word limits guide the length and depth of your writing.
The format changes depending on whether you write a notice or an article.

quiz.say: Which element is essential for a notice but not always for an article?
quiz.why: The issuing authority name is a key part of the formal structure of a notice.

wrong.1: The date is needed for both, so this is not the best answer.
wrong.2: Articles also need a title, so this is not unique to notices.
wrong.3: Notices do not typically have a formal conclusion section.

quiz.say: If a word limit is 80 words, and you write 120 words, what is the main issue?

options.show: The writing is too long and lacks focus.
options.say: The writing is too long and lacks focus.

quiz.why: Exceeding the limit suggests you have included unnecessary details or repeated ideas.

wrong.1: Tone relates to feeling, not length, so this is incorrect.
wrong.2: Format is about structure, not the total word count.
wrong.3: A weak introduction is a content issue, not a length issue.

quiz.say: When writing an article, what should the conclusion do?

options.show: Ask a question to the reader.
options.say: Ask a question to the reader.

quiz.why: The conclusion wraps up the article by reminding the reader of the key ideas discussed.

wrong.0: Introducing new topics here confuses the reader and breaks the flow.
wrong.1: While possible, the main job is summarizing, not questioning.
wrong.2: History belongs in the body paragraphs, not the final summary.
